cards.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church in Corinth, a church arguing over who they follow (1 Corinthians 1:1-2, 12). He just told them the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing (1 Corinthians 1:18). Now he looks back at the day he first came to them.

cards.question: When Paul first came to the church in Corinth, how does he say he came?

cards.text: No polished speech, no big words, friend, and Paul did it ON PURPOSE. He made up his mind what he'd focus on the whole time he was with them.

cards.question: What did Paul resolve to know while he was with the church in Corinth?

answers.text: Nothing except Jesus Christ and Him crucified
Nothing except the Law and the Prophets
Nothing except the wisdom of the Greeks

cards.text: Now Paul gets real about how he was feeling when he walked into Corinth. Brace yourself, friend.

cards.question: Paul says he came to the church in Corinth feeling calm and confident. True or false?

cards.text: Nope, Paul came in weakness and fear, with much trembling. PAUL had the shakes, friend, and here I thought I was the only one who trembled before a big batch!

cards.question: Paul's message and preaching weren't built on persuasive words of wisdom. What came with them instead?

answers.text: A demonstration of the Spirit's power

cards.question: Paul preached that way so the faith of the church in Corinth would rest on God's ___ and not on men's wisdom.

cards.text: Then Paul turns a corner: among the mature, they DO speak a message of wisdom. Read close here, friend, because I'm the stamper who skimmed one recipe and set the timer for fifty minutes instead of fifteen.

cards.question: The message of wisdom Paul speaks among the mature is the wisdom of this age. True or false?

cards.text: Right, not the wisdom of this age or of its rulers, who are coming to nothing. Paul speaks of the mysterious and hidden wisdom of God.

cards.question: When did God destine His mysterious and hidden wisdom for our glory?

answers.text: After the rulers came to nothing

cards.text: Now Paul looks at the rulers of this age, the people in charge. None of them understood God's hidden wisdom.

cards.question: Paul says that if the rulers of this age had understood God's wisdom, they would not have done something. What?

answers.text: Burned the scroll of the prophet

cards.text: Paul goes on, as it is written: “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no heart has imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him.”

cards.question: No eye has seen what God has prepared for those who love Him. So how does Paul say "we" know about it?

answers.text: God revealed it to us by the Spirit
We worked it out by careful study
An angel explained it to us in a dream

cards.text: The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God. ALL things, friend, and I lived in a junk drawer for YEARS and never once found the bottom of it!
Then Paul compares it to people: who knows a man's thoughts except his own spirit within him? Which is great news, because nobody needs to know how many times a day I count my chocolate chips.

cards.question: In the same way, Paul says, no one knows the thoughts of God except the ___ of God.
Paul says "we" have not received the spirit of the world but the Spirit who is from God. Why?

answers.text: So we may understand what God has freely given us
So we can win every argument with the wise
So we will be praised by the rulers of this age

cards.question: When Paul speaks about what God has freely given, he uses words taught by human wisdom. True or false?

cards.text: Right, words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual truths in spiritual words. Then Paul turns to the natural man, who does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God.

cards.question: To the natural man, what are the things that come from the Spirit of God?

cards.text: Foolishness, the same word for how the message of the cross looks to those who are perishing (1 Corinthians 1:18). It's like handing somebody a recipe card in a language they can't read, and they squint at YOU like you're the one who's confused.

cards.question: The natural man cannot understand the things of the Spirit of God, because they are ___ discerned.
Paul says the spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is subject to everyone's judgment. True or false?

cards.text: Then Paul quotes: “For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” Picture somebody walking up to the Lord Himself with a few suggestions, friend, YEAH, NO.

cards.question: No one has known the mind of the Lord so as to instruct Him. But what does Paul say "we" have?

cards.text: The mind of Christ, friend, and I'm over here proud when I remember where I hung my apron. Stay close, because Paul's got plenty more to say to this church, and this letter's NOT done.
